attributes.commissioned_by: the Wardenry, as a routine re-levelling after crust movement. Nobody asked for borings.
attributes.finding: fresh water under the centre of the plain, at a depth ordinary gear can reach
attributes.not_filed: no fair copy was ever entered on the College roll. The house rule is that a finding goes on the roll before it goes to the body that commissioned it — surveyor, ground, date, one line of result — and the entry would have gone out with the spring caravan and been on the roll at the far rim by autumn. Denet sealed the packet instead. The RR 203 roll carries no line against his name, and the forty-one leaves in the packet are the whole of the record.
attributes.period: RR 201 to RR 203 — two summers. The packet was sealed in the spring of RR 203.
attributes.still_unopened: the packet itself has not been opened by anyone, at Bell Harrow or anywhere else
attributes.what_the_survey_could_not_say: how much of it there is. Borings give you a depth and a quality, not a volume. Reachable is not the same as plentiful, and the packet does not claim it is.
attributes.who_knows: Denet, who wrote it. Oreth Vask, who has known about a month by way of the Assembly's own channels and not by way of Denet. Nobody at the College: no clerk took an entry, because none was ever offered.
attributes.why_it_starts_the_book: a survey is not a rumour. A rumour can be waited out; a survey has to be answered. And because it was never filed, it can also be bought, or burned — which is what makes it worth doing either.

name: The Levelling of the Centre
summary: The Wardenry commissioned a routine re-levelling of the centre routes after two seasons of crust movement and sent Denet Rasca, who was thorough. Across two summers he ran borings nobody had asked for, read them against a College water-glass, and found fresh water under the middle of the plain at a depth ordinary gear could reach. In the spring of RR 203 he stitched the leaves into a packet and struck both seals over the thread without first entering a fair copy on the College roll, which his seal obliged him to do. He has carried the only copy since, and has not decided what it is for.
